caption:
India's battery storage capacity just grew 941% in three months. Not over a decade. In a single quarter.

India added 4.6 GWh of battery energy storage capacity in Q1 2026, up 941% from the previous quarter. Cumulative capacity is projected to grow to 346 GWh by 2033, up from under 1 GWh today.

Battery storage is what lets solar and wind power actually run at night and on cloudy days - without it, renewable energy has a hard ceiling. Rajasthan leads with 42% of installed capacity, followed by Gujarat and Maharashtra, the same states already leading India's solar buildout.

The market is expected to grow from $2 billion this year to $8.6 billion by 2031 - a sector barely anyone was building five years ago.

This isn't a side project to solar power. It's the piece that decides whether renewable energy actually works at scale, or just looks good on paper.

Sources: Mercom India, IBEF, ESS News (2026)
